title: Dow Edges Higher as S&P 500, Nasdaq Slip Post‑Nvidia Surge; Dell Earnings Await【Live Updates】
body:
Wall Street opened Tuesday on a cautiously optimistic note, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average nudging higher while the broader S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite slipped after the explosive rally sparked by Nvidia’s 31 percent surge on Monday. Investors were also eyeing Dell Technologies’ earnings report, slated for later in the day, to gauge whether the PC‑maker can sustain its recent turnaround amid lingering supply‑chain headwinds.  

The Dow rose about 0.3 percent, adding roughly 100 points as defensive heavyweight stocks such as UnitedHealth Group and Procter & Gamble helped offset the pullback in technology‑heavy indices. The S&P 500, however, fell close to 0.4 percent, and the Nasdaq slipped nearly 0.7 percent, erasing a portion of the gains that had vaulted the Nasdaq to record highs after Nvidia’s earnings blew past expectations. Analysts said the modest retreat reflects a classic profit‑taking move rather than a fundamental shift in market sentiment. “After a day of almost irrational exuberance, traders are re‑balancing,” noted Karen Liu, senior market strategist at Global Insights. “The tech sector is still the engine, but investors are now looking for confirmation that the rally is sustainable.”  

Nvidia’s meteoric rise, driven by a staggering 31 percent jump in its share price following an earnings beat and bullish guidance on artificial‑intelligence demand, remains the centerpiece of today’s market narrative. The chipmaker’s performance has lifted the Nasdaq’s AI‑related sub‑index by more than 10 percent over the past week, prompting a wave of speculative buying in smaller AI‑focused firms. Yet some market participants warn that the surge may have outpaced the underlying fundamentals. “Valuations are now in the stratosphere,” said Michael Patel, equity analyst at Meridian Capital. “If Nvidia’s guidance proves overly optimistic, we could see a sharp correction across the tech sector.”  

In contrast, the industrial and consumer‑discretionary segments showed relative resilience. Companies such as Caterpillar and Home Depot posted modest gains, buoyed by strong demand for construction equipment and home‑improvement goods, respectively. The energy sector also saw a lift, with crude oil prices edging higher on concerns about supply disruptions in the Middle East. This mixed backdrop helped the Dow stay in positive territory, underscoring the index’s broader composition of non‑tech heavyweights.  

Dell Technologies, a key earnings driver for the day, is expected to deliver mixed results. The company posted a 12 percent revenue increase in its most recent quarter, driven by higher demand for its XPS laptops and a rebound in server sales. However, analysts remain wary of lingering inventory challenges and the competitive pressure from rivals such as HP and Lenovo. “Dell’s outlook will be a litmus test for the broader PC market’s health,” said Sofia Martinez, technology analyst at Brightline Research. “If they can sustain margin expansion while navigating component shortages, it could reinforce confidence in the sector’s recovery.”  

Looking ahead, investors will monitor several catalysts that could shape market direction over the next few weeks. The Federal Reserve’s upcoming policy meeting, scheduled for next Thursday, will be closely watched for any hints about the timing of interest‑rate adjustments. Meanwhile, the earnings calendar remains packed, with major names such as Amazon, Alphabet and Tesla slated to report later in the month. The interplay between AI‑driven growth stories and macro‑economic headwinds will likely dictate whether the market can maintain its upward trajectory or succumb to a broader pullback. For now, the modest rise in the Dow suggests that while enthusiasm for tech remains high, traders are exercising prudence as they await further data points to confirm the durability of this rally.
